items.title: The Problem of Pattern and Scale in Ecology: The Robert H. MacArthur Award Lecture
items.summary: It is argued that the problem of pattern and scale is the central problem in ecology, unifying population biology and ecosystems science, and marrying basic and applied ecology. Applied challenges, such as the prediction of the ecological causes and consequences of global climate change, require the interfacing of phenomena that occur on very different scales of space, time, and ecological organization. items.title: Executive Function Decay: Why Managerial Judgment Fails Under Pressure and How Organizations Can Respond
items.summary: Mental-health strain has become a routine feature of organizational life, yet managers and organizations continue to struggle to explain why capable employees make avoidable errors, why teams lose coordination under pressure, and why judgment quality deteriorates during periods of sustained stress. items.title: Perceptual symbol systems
items.summary: Prior to the twentieth century, theories of knowledge were inherently perceptual. Since then, developments in logic, statistics, and programming languages have inspired amodal theories that rest on principles fundamentally different from those underlying perception. In addition, perceptual approaches have become widely viewed as untenable because they are assumed to implement recording systems, not conceptual systems. items.summary: The cerebellum is an ancient brain component, conserved across mammalian species, that has classically played roles in regulating muscle tone, limb coordination, and equilibrium, as well as in non-motor functions, such as language, cognition, and emotion. items.title: SPINOZA’S THEORY OF MODES AND THE RELATIONAL ONTOLOGY OF NETWORK NEUROSCIENCE
items.summary: Network neuroscience explains the function of a neural region by its position within a connectome rather than by its intrinsic properties. This paper argues that this explanatory practice is tacitly committed to a relational ontology: the thesis that a neural system's properties are constituted by, not merely correlated with, the relations among its parts, which the science relies on but does not articulate. items.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation combined with soft robotic glove training improves upper-limb motor function after subacute stroke: a randomized controlled pilot trial
items.summary: Background Upper-limb dysfunction, particularly impaired distal hand function, remains one of the most disabling sequelae following a stroke. Soft robotic glove (SRG) training can provide repetitive and task-specific hand practice; however, its therapeutic effects may be limited by insufficient modulation of the damaged motor network. items.summary: Introduction Affective prosody, the expression of emotion through speech, is often disrupted in dementia of the Alzheimer’s type (DAT), yet its acoustic and neural bases remain poorly understood. Extending our earlier single-group investigation, we compared individuals with DAT and cognitively healthy older adults across speech acoustics, prefrontal activation, and their coupling. items.title: The Thermodynamic Constraints of Memory: Evaluating Synaptic Plasticity and Long-Term Potentiation through the Lens of Mass and Energy Conservation
items.summary: This article is about how human memory is not an invisible, magical thing, but a concrete physical structure made of matter and bound by the strict laws of physics. Specifically, it bridges two completely different worlds: molecular neuroscience (how brain cells connect) and classical physics (the Law of Conservation of Mass and Thermodynamics).

items.title: Case Report: A novel hemizygous nonsense variant in PPP1R3F gene associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder
items.summary: Background PPP1R3F deficiency syndrome is an extremely rare, recently identified X-linked recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. It is caused by hemizygous variants in the PPP1R3F gene, which encodes a glycogen-targeting subunit of the brain-specific protein phosphatase 1 (PP1). Dysfunction of PPP1R3F disrupts glycogen metabolism in astrocytes, leading to insufficient energy supply to synapses during critical periods of brain development and subsequently causing neurodevelopmental abnormalities. items.title: Neural Remodeling Across Cancer Evolution: Temporal, Spatial, Cellular, and Functional Principles of Tumor–Nerve Ecosystems
items.summary: Cancer neuroscience now asks not only whether tumors contain nerves, but how neural architecture, neuronal and glial states, and neural output change through cancer evolution. This critical narrative review integrates evidence from precursor lesions, primary tumors, invasion, metastasis, and treatment-associated states, while distinguishing neural remodeling from axonogenesis, neurogenesis, perineural invasion, and direct synaptic integration. items.summary: Abstract The microstructure of cells within human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of cortex with its unique function. While fine-scale relative to a cell, these changes at population level impact architectural properties of cortex measurable in vivo by noninvasive MRI, such as the thickness and myelin content of cortex. items.summary: Background In cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG)-based driving-fatigue detection, most existing decoders are designed around second-scale short windows, whereas fatigue is a slow drift; short-window spectral features provide little direct evidence of that slow drift, limiting fatigue decisions. items.title: Vigorous physical activity relates to rumination and perseveration in college students
items.summary: Abstract Recent reports suggest that mental health concerns such as depression and anxiety are at all-time high levels in college students. Perseverative cognitions such as rumination, perseveration, and worry are generally related to worse mental health outcomes. In contrast, physical activity (PA) engagement relates to better mental health. However, the relationship between physical activity and perseverative cognitions is not well understood. items.title: Retinography as a marker of the progression of cognitive impairment and/or dementia in older people with type II diabetes mellitus
items.summary: Introduction The aging population increases type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) prevalence and consequently heightens related complications, including dementia and microvascular disease. This study examined the relationship between diabetic retinopathy (DR) and cognitive decline in adults with T2DM. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted with 328 individuals aged ≥60 years with T2DM in Córdoba, Spain. items.title: The evolution of shared worlds: teaching and the origins of cumulative culture
items.summary: The emergence of cumulative culture marks a fundamental transformation in the history of human living. Through cultural practices, ways of doing, making, and relating persist across generations and become progressively transformed. Yet culture does not persist because knowledge or representations are transmitted from one individual to another. It persists because human beings participate in recurrent forms of coordination that become part of their histories of living together. items.summary: Introduction As previous research suggests, self-compassion may be an effective way of managing pain and protecting against mental health disorders in patients struggling with chronic pain. On the other hand, the role of emotional well-being in these relationships remains unexplained. Based on the broaden-and-build theory of positive emotions, this study assumed that self-kindness can be indirectly related to pain intensity and anxiety via positive and negative affect. items.title: Leadership Development through Experience (70-20-10 Model): A Critical Examination and Reconceptualization
items.summary: The 70-20-10 model of leadership development, which posits that learning is derived 70% from challenging experiences, 20% from developmental relationships, and 10% from formal coursework, has become a cornerstone of corporate training and development strategy. Despite its widespread adoption, the model rests on a surprisingly fragile empirical foundation and is often applied with a rigid prescriptivism that belies its origins as a descriptive framework. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk.
